sources.title: The effectiveness of malaria camps as part of the malaria control program in Odisha, India
sources.type: Primary quasi-experimental evaluation; final published article, superseding the January 2023 preprint
sources.inspected: HTML Introduction; Results/Study population; Discussion; Methods/costing; affiliations and acknowledgements. Not a raw-data reanalysis.
locators: Results: Study population and study design
Methods: Costing study design, data collection, and analyses
sources.usable_summary: The paper dates programme implementation to 2017. Its 2019–20 evaluation enrolled 2,463 people in 15 villages in Keonjhar and Jharsuguda, not Malkangiri. New-camp villages had lower adjusted odds of PCR-detected infection relative to delayed-camp villages at final follow-up. Non-random assignment, pandemic disruption and follow-up limitations prevent causal inference. The paper documents planning, village volunteers, ASHA training, mobilisation and follow-up alongside testing. This evaluates a collective programme, not the film.
sources.perspective_limit: Government programme staff coauthored the study alongside university and hospital researchers; describe as peer-reviewed evaluation, not wholly independent of implementation.
sources.proposed_addition: A published evaluation followed malaria camps in 15 villages in Keonjhar and Jharsuguda during 2019–20. It found an association with reduced infection, while its authors cautioned that the study design and pandemic disruption prevented a causal conclusion. This is evidence about the programme, not evidence that the film changed health outcomes.
sources.chronology_addition: The film’s 2015 setting should remain distinct from the programme, which the published evaluation dates to 2017.

sources.title: Community Healthcare Providers’ Perspective on Malaria Control in Difficult Terrains (DAMaN) in Odisha, India
sources.type: Primary qualitative interviews with health workers, not a film-reception study
sources.inspected: Publisher metadata/abstract and extracted full-text PDF, especially printed pp.56,60–63. Web screenshots failed (cache miss); no visual page inspection claimed.
locators: p.60 Data Collection, Management and Analysis
p.62 volunteer follow-up and collaboration paragraphs
sources.usable_summary: Interviews with 53 workers in five districts, conducted April–August 2024, describe perceived access improvements alongside road difficulties, workload, supply constraints and inconvenient camp timing. Volunteers organise camps and support follow-up. Malkangiri was not included. Interviewers and several authors worked in malaria programmes; participants were workers, not a representative resident sample. Do not convert their observations into measured outcomes or community consensus.
sources.proposed_addition: Health workers bring another perspective. In interviews published in 2025, workers described roads, staffing, supplies and camp schedules as practical barriers. They also sought support for volunteers’ work between camps. Their accounts locate care in repeated collective labour rather than a single act of rescue.
sources.critical_notes: Use only attributed operational testimony. The article has inconsistent submission/acceptance dates and author spellings between byline and citation template; cite Pradhan et al. It makes broad health-effect claims beyond its qualitative design. Do not repeat those as independently measured facts.

strengths: Clearly separates award year from film year.
Credits ASHA, anganwadi and other staff in filmmaker testimony.
Already distinguishes government service counts from effects of the film.
Does not claim a fresh full-film viewing.
precise_changes: Add programme date explicitly in body, retaining distinction between 2015 fictional setting and later programme history. Existing 2016–17 fiscal-year government reporting can be reconciled as planning/initial reporting rather than silently forcing one date.
Replace or substantiate the general paragraph about superstition with the attributed worker findings above. Do not imply the film exclusively depicts a lone saviour without full-film analysis.
Describe 1,817 camps and 514,761 screenings as service activity, not infections averted or causal impact.
Add the evaluation briefly, without medical recommendations or converting odds into percentage-point reductions.
current_draft_assessment.editorial_priority: Two short sourced paragraphs can add concrete fairness and evidential depth without turning a cinema essay into programme advocacy.

unfilled_gaps: No direct Malkangiri resident or Adivasi audience account of the film was secured. Worker interviews cannot fill this gap.
Panchayati Raj member study located (2024;56(2):45–52; publisher URL below), but full text was not accessible in this pass; search snippet is not adequate for substantive claims.
No evidence that the film itself changed malaria prevalence, service uptake or public policy.
No fresh full-film viewing: neither endorsement nor rejection of particular scenes is warranted from this research.
Chronology needs source-specific phrasing: government reporting uses fiscal 2016–17 while published evaluation says implementation in 2017; do not imply the film’s 2015 narrative dates the programme.
